steps.body: A number reached earlier in the count is less. Three is fewer than five, so 3 is less than 5.
steps.narration: A number reached earlier in the count is less. Three is fewer than five, so 3 is less than 5.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 12? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 12 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 11.
10 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 12 to reach 11.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 12: you land on 11.
widget.successFeedback: 11 — one hop back, and one hop earlier in the song always means less.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 12 reaches 11.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 12 means a single hop back, stopping on 11.

predict.reveal: Earlier in the counting song means less, and 4 arrives three steps before 7 — wherever two numbers sit in the song, the earlier one is the smaller, however far apart they stand.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm less numeral.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm less numeral uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

concept.body: Less and greater are two views of one fact: if 4 is less than 7, then 7 is greater than 4 — both at once.
concept.narration: Less and greater are two views of one fact: if 4 is less than 7, then 7 is greater than 4 — both at once.
